key_insight: FERMAT shows that the best prediction approach depends on the task: representation-based methods work better for future disease risk, while generation-based methods are stronger for same-day clinical event prediction.
clinical_relevance: This suggests clinical foundation models may need to combine both prediction styles to better support risk stratification and near-term event forecasting in real-world EHR settings.
method: Trained a 65M-parameter autoregressive clinical foundation model on longitudinal EHRs from 3.77 million patients.
Compared representation-based predictors with generation-based forecasts across disease risk and clinical event tasks.
Evaluated performance on chronic kidney disease, fatty liver, diabetes, and same-day diagnoses, prescriptions, and procedures.
evidence_signal: In a 10,000-patient test cohort, representation-based prediction improved five-year disease-risk AUROC by 0.098-0.115, while generation-based prediction reached 71.0% Recall@10 for same-day events versus 55.7% for representation-based methods.
watch_item: Results come from a single-hospital EHR dataset, so performance may not generalize across health systems or documentation practices.
paper_title: FERMAT: An Autoregressive Clinical Foundation Model for Disease Risk and Clinical Event Prediction
